scope.items_are: outward-facing changes only — project-internal maintenance (repo upkeep, convention changes, documentation updates) never becomes an item. This is a scoping rule about what counts as an item, enforced in the schema and the agent guidelines; it is NOT a trimming rule and there is no filter for it in the validator.
scope.intel_brewfile: out of this tool entirely; I-17 checks it
scope.deterministic_layer: validates, normalizes, counts, buckets, calculates impact. Never deletes, trims or re-rates.

memory_proposals.bucket_rule: memory proposals do not force `attention`; action proposals do. `watch-item` and `method-note` propose changes to what we remember, `edit` and `structural` to the user's system — only the latter needs a decision. Every axis that can pre-accept (compute_impact, compute_risk_level, compute_initial_bucket, W-ATTENTION-NOSUG) asks `needs_a_decision`, a NEGATION, so a kind outside the vocabulary demands a decision rather than reading as a memory proposal.

method-note.method_topic: what the note is about, in a few words
method-note.method_note: the instruction itself, written to read sensibly when copied verbatim into the next run's context
method-note.rationale: the failure the ordinary research path already produced here

watch-item.watch_topic: the short phrase a future run matches against its changelog
watch-item.watch_note: the context that lets a future hit explain itself without re-deriving everything
watch-item.rationale: your answers to the self-test, in your own words

self_test_failed.rule: The self-test TAGS, never removes. A failing proposal is still written; convergence reviews every tagged one and verifies that dropping it is appropriate. A proposal the agent never writes is one convergence cannot restore.
self_test_failed.on_a_non_memory_kind: E-FIELD-TYPE — the tag is present iff the kind is a memory kind

research_keys.unrecognized: E-RESEARCH-UNKNOWNKEY — the value is quarantined verbatim and the tool is held for review

degradation.rule: a non-empty content_losing forces `attention` and clears `pre_accept`; every other finding is a marker on the card and changes no bucket

clause_order: 0. content_losing(view) is non-empty -> attention   [D1 - above the source clause on purpose]
1. source in NON_VERSION_SOURCES -> routine if expected else attention
2. security_tier(view) is not None -> security_auto if the stored tier is valid and tier in ACCEPTED_TIERS (P1, P2, P3) else security_mixed   [G-SEC - P0 and held tools are never in the auto strip]

2b. has_security and security_only and impact == "none" and version_delta not in (major, unknown) and runnable and not pre_accept_bars(view) -> security_auto   [pre-G-SEC, unchanged: D2/E3 - a barred tool falls through to security_mixed]
4. risk_level elevated, or config needs_attention, or an edit/structural suggestion (items.needs_a_decision), or not runnable -> attention
bucketing.d2_routing: clause-2b guard (orchestrator ruling, overriding the spec's variants A and B): a barred security-only tool falls through to security_mixed — never to attention (A), and never left in security_auto with a cleared checkbox (B). security_mixed already renders an expanded card with an 'affects this setup' badge and correct counters; anything downstream of finalize_tool desyncs the Overview tiles. Since CONTRACT 4 D2 governs every tool that is NOT G-SEC — including one whose only security content is not a positively identified fix.
bucketing.g_sec_routing: a version-source tool with a positively identified security fix (security.nature == fix, grounded by I-21) or a vendor-declared unread security release is G-SEC: security_tier(view) computes its display priority (P0-P3) and its acceptance holds once, the validator stores it, and clause 2 routes it — an accepted tier (P1, P2, P3) to security_auto, P0 and held to security_mixed. D2's elevated bar and the reaches limb do not apply to it; the priority panel is the visibility D2 asked for. enum-invalid and container-unreadable bar every tool, G-SEC or not (R7).

pre_accept.predicate: sug is baseline AND auto_runnable AND items.accepts_baseline(tool) — one predicate for assembly and convergence, reading security_tier (key required: null or an object), pre_accept_bars (key required: the EXPORTED bars, never recomputed), the bucket, risk_level and forced_conservative. Not G-SEC (security_tier null): bucket != "attention" AND risk_level == "low" AND not content_losing AND pre_accept_bars == [] AND not forced_conservative. G-SEC: the tier is valid AND tier in ACCEPTED_TIERS AND not content_losing AND pre_accept_bars == [] AND not forced_conservative. A malformed tier ({} included) is never accepted. The bars and the tier are the VALIDATOR'S, copied by finalize_tool — assembly never recomputes them from assembled items, which can hold synthesized reaching security items the bucket never saw
pre_accept.bars_source: the validator's view — the validator stores view.pre_accept_bars (a G-SEC view's are its tier's P0 reasons and holds, read off the stored tier), finalize_tool COPIES it onto the tool, and accepts_baseline refuses (KeyError) a tool nobody computed them for rather than recomputing from assembled items

required-edit.text: Needs you — a config change is required before this upgrade works

pinned.text: Needs you — pinned; lift the pin to take the fix

incompatible-unfixed.text: Needs you — breaks something here; no config fix proposed

edit-proposed.text: Accepted — config edits proposed, not applied unless you accept them

config-attention.text: Accepted — config needs attention — no edit proposed

relevant-fix.text: Accepted — the fix touches how you use it

fix-with-breaking.text: Accepted — also has a breaking change that reaches this machine: take a look

fix-with-risk.text: Accepted — also carries a risk here

vendor-unread.text: Accepted — vendor declares a security release without details

fix-with-breaking-unseen.text: Accepted — breaking change, not seen here

fix.text: Accepted — a security fix, nothing flagged for this setup

shape.reasons: array<reason>, fixed order — every reason that holds
shape.holds: array<hold>, fixed order — every hold that applies
shape.ids: {reason or hold: [item or suggestion id]} — [] for tool-level ones

precedence: applicability: >=1 item is_positive_fix, or vendor_silent_categories contains security; else security_tier is null (not G-SEC)
priority: the highest level with a reason — computed WITHOUT the holds
tier: P0 if priority is P0; else held if any hold; else the priority
a held tool keeps its priority on the page (R1) and is never counted as accepted

usage_file_kinds.other: anything else — no line is an install declaration; a #-led line is still a comment

supersedes: D2 elevated bar for G-SEC tools

suggestion_fields.name: requirement
suggestion_fields.note: required|proposed — on an action suggestion (edit, structural, or any unrecognized kind); read by nothing on a memory or upgrade suggestion

suggestion_fields.name: serves
suggestion_fields.note: the items this edit answers: the part of the derived item id after `#` (`cve:CVE-2026-1234`, `slug:krun-arm`) or the full id

suggestion_fields.name: serves_item_ids
suggestion_fields.note: `serves` resolved against the tool's item ids; the original stays verbatim. No convergence op can write it

watch_hit.grounded_against: {session_dir}/watch-items.json — a copy of the machine-global store, taken when {{STANDING_NOTES}} is filled
watch_hit.topic_match: exact, after .strip(); no case folding and no fuzzy match

highlight.scored: grounded hits only — the view's watch_hit_item_ids export. An ungrounded, malformed or unchecked hit bars pre-acceptance (fail-closed) but earns no prominence

watch_hit.distinct_from: memory_proposals.watch_topic/watch_note, which PROPOSE a watch item on a suggestion; watch_hit says an existing one FIRED, on an item

global.filled_by: promotion during convergence only — never a per-tool proposal (schemas.md §1.7b Scope)
global.why_not_a_third_file: a tool id always contains a colon, so this key cannot collide with one; the store then rides along in the method-notes snapshot every reader already takes, instead of needing a third one

fields.name: body
fields.note: the detail: why/how. Overflow from title lands here

fields.name: local.evidence
fields.required: yes if local present, may be []

fields.name: local.evidence[].role
fields.note: usage|install|reference — on an object-form entry; absent makes no usage claim

fields.name: local.evidence[].quote
fields.note: a VERBATIM excerpt of the whole line(s) showing the use (I-23)

fields.name: security.nature
fields.note: fix|boundary|unclear — only a GROUNDED fix (I-21) makes a tool G-SEC

fields.name: watch_hit
fields.note: set iff this item answers a stored watch item for this tool

fields.name: watch_hit.topic
fields.note: VERBATIM copy of the stored watch item's `topic`

item_sort_key: negated severity rank (worst first; unknown severity last)
direction rank (reaches, unclear, does_not_reach, no local block)
effect rank (risk, none, benefit, no local block)
id ascending — the tiebreak that makes the order total

flags.on_disagreement: the validator's value wins; E-FLAG-DISAGREE is raised

security_display.predicate: rating == critical, or exploited_in_wild, or local.direction == reaches, or severity in (warning, incompatible)

E-ANCHOR-MALFORMED.summary: `anchor.value` does not match its kind's grammar

E-CITE-KIND.summary: a citation kind is outside the vocabulary

E-CITE-URL.summary: a citation url is not an absolute http(s) URL

E-ENTRY-NOID.summary: a research entry has no usable string id

E-ENTRY-NOTOBJECT.summary: a research entry is not an object

E-ENUM-INVALID.summary: a field's value is outside its closed vocabulary

E-EVID-MALFORMED.summary: an evidence entry is not a path

E-FIELD-TYPE.summary: a field has the wrong type

E-FLAG-DISAGREE.summary: a checker-emitted flag disagrees with recomputation

E-FLAG-FORBIDDEN.summary: a checker emitted a validator-only flag

E-INTEL-BREWFILE.summary: intel.Brewfile is out of this tool entirely

E-ITEM-DUP-ANCHOR.summary: two items in one tool derive one id

E-REQUIREMENT-CONTRADICTED.summary: a `proposed` edit serving an `incompatible` item — it reads `required`

E-RESEARCH-NOTARRAY.summary: a research file is not a JSON array

E-RESEARCH-UNKNOWNKEY.summary: a research object carries a top-level key outside the closed set (kept in quarantine)

E-RESEARCH-UNREADABLE.summary: a research file could not be read

E-SEC-BLOCK-ORPHAN.summary: `security` block on an item not tagged `security`

E-SEC-FIX-UNGROUNDED.summary: `security.nature: fix` without the `security` tag, a `security` block and a cited `change`

E-STRUCT-PRECOND.summary: a structural op's precondition does not hold

E-SUG-REQUIRED-UNGROUNDED.summary: a `required` edit that serves no resolved `incompatible` item

E-SUG-SERVES-UNRESOLVED.summary: a `serves` entry naming no item of this tool

E-TAG-NONE.summary: no recognized tag on the item

E-TAG-UNKNOWN.summary: a tag outside the closed set (kept verbatim)

E-USAGE-UNGROUNDED.summary: a `usage` evidence entry that does not resolve, cannot be read, or whose `quote` is absent or not in the file

E-VALIDATOR-CRASH.summary: a validator stage failed on this tool; it is kept with what conformed

E-WATCH-HIT-NOLOCAL.summary: a watch-item hit with no `local` block

E-WATCH-HIT-UNGROUNDED.summary: `watch_hit.topic` names no stored watch item for this tool

W-ENTRY-DUPLICATE.summary: two research entries claim one tool id

W-ENTRY-UNMATCHED.summary: a research entry names no collected candidate

W-EVID-ROOT.summary: an evidence path resolves only under an unconfigured repo

W-MEMBER-QUARANTINED.summary: a wrong-typed array member was quarantined, not dropped

W-SEC-FIX-NOID.summary: a grounded fix with no CVE, advisory or anchored id

W-SHAPE-COERCED.summary: a field was the wrong shape and was coerced

W-STRUCT-UNCHECKED.summary: a structural precondition could not be checked

W-SUG-DUP-ID.summary: a suggestion id is not unique across the report

W-TITLE-LONG.summary: title is longer than the glanceable bar; detail belongs in body

W-USAGE-INSTALL-ONLY.summary: a `usage` quote whose every occurrence lies on the tool's own install declaration or on comment lines

W-WATCH-HIT-UNRAISED.summary: a watch-item hit left at `info`; a watched topic earns at least `notable`

W-WATCH-UNCHECKED.summary: a watch-item hit could not be checked against the stored watch items

anchor_grammars.none: value must be null; a non-empty `slug` is required instead
